reading.body:
CyrusOne's AUS2-AUS3 campus in Austin publishes 19 MW of IT capacity across two facilities and 242,000 square feet of technical space. At a conservative 40 kW per rack, this is roughly 475 racks, though AI training workloads can reach 60–80 kW per rack, which would yield 240–320 racks. The campus holds general-purpose security certifications including PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and FISMA, qualifying it for regulated workloads but not uniquely for AI infrastructure.

Among Texas's 19 facilities with published capacity figures, this campus ranks tenth, representing four percent of the state's 475 MW of disclosed data center IT load. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities in total, the vast majority of which publish no capacity data, so published rankings reflect only a fraction of actual deployment and do not indicate market dominance within the state.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on grid headroom and power pricing not given here. The published IT load is modest compared to dedicated hyperscaler campuses now exceeding 100 MW per site. No information is published about available power, water cooling, grid interconnection timeline, or whether capacity is spoken for.
